routes.label: Recover the hypotenuse from the tangent ratio

answerCheck.reason: Cos θ = 1 - 2sin²(θ/2) = 1/x. Since θ is acute, x > 1 and tan²θ = (1 - cos²θ)/cos²θ = x² - 1. Thus tan θ = √(x² - 1).
Factoring gives x-intercepts (-5,0) and (3,0), while B=(0,-15). The two angles beside the upward vertical at B have tangents 5/15=1/3 and 3/15=1/5. Therefore tan(∠ABC)=(1/3+1/5)/(1-(1/3)(1/5))=4/7.

routes.label: Find cosine using a dot product

answerCheck.reason: ABC has area 49√3, so each added triangle has area 14√3 and height 2√3. Put the center at the origin and A=(-7,-7√3/3). The common radius is 14/√3, giving D=(-3,-13√3/3), with the negative horizontal coordinate fixed by 0<θ<60°. Thus cos θ=(154/3)/(196/3)=11/14 and sin θ=5√3/14, so tan θ=5√3/11.
